newsitem.title: USA: Texas separatist shot dead, leader indicted.
newsitem.headline: Texas separatist shot dead, leader indicted.

text.p: Police on Monday shot and killed one of two members of the Republic of Texas militia holed up in the west Texas mountains since a week-long stand-off with police ended over the weekend, police said.

The two men, who walked out of the separatist group's compound hours before Republic leader Richard McLaren signed a ceasefire agreement and surrendered on Saturday, were found hiding near the group's Davis Mountains compound, police said.
Police did not immediately identify the dead man and his companion was still at large following a brief shoot-out with police tracking them on horseback and in helicopters overhead.
"A Justice of the Peace has been called to pronounce him dead. We can't confirm his identity at this time," police spokeswoman Sherri Deatherage Green said. "The other suspect is still at large."

A pack of 30 bloodhounds closed in on the two men -- identified as Mike Matson, 48, and Richard Keyes, 21 -- as they were holed up about a mile (1.6 km) from the compound in Davis Mountain Resorts, a rural subdivision near Fort Davis.

The fugitive separatists were dressed in camouflage and armed with an assault rifle, a deer-hunting rifle and a .9mm pistol. Keyes is wanted on state kidnapping charges and Matson is wanted for questioning, police said.

McLaren, 43, the self-styled ambassador of the ragtag group, was indicted on Monday on federal fraud and conspiracy charges for allegedly issuing $1.8 billion in worthless financial warrants to militia members, federal prosecutors said.
McLaren and his wife Evelyn McLaren, 50, were charged in a 25-count indictment with bank fraud, mail fraud and conspiracy for their roles in the scheme, U.S. Attorney Paul Coggins said.

"These defendants are not proud Texans but paper terrorists, they are not revolutionaries but rip-off artists, they are not patriots but parasites. In short, they are bullies," Coggins said. "Our message to bullies is: don't mess with Texas."

The McLarens and four other Republic of Texas members surrendered on Saturday after a standoff with police in the west Texas mountains sparked by the arrest of one of the group's members on state firearms charges.

McLaren and his followers, who claim Texas is an independent nation, had vowed to defend their "embassy" compound to the death but surrendered when scores of police surrounded them and prepared to move in.
